prompt: Use case: illustration-story / identity-preserving animation key poses. Make a production sprite atlas for an offline children's learning app. Polished friendly storybook animal illustration with soft shaded fur/feathers/scales, clear anatomy and expressive eyes, matching the reference style. ONE animal identity reused in ALL cells, camera/head size/body proportions/markings EXACTLY consistent. Every pose is full body, no cropped limbs. All face RIGHT unless subject says front-facing. Genuine transparent background, NO coloured paper/background, floor, panels, labels, letters, numbers, arrows, speech bubbles, motion lines, cast shadows or decorative objects. Equal square grid cells with 8% safe margins, consistent scale, same notional ground baseline 85% down each cell for grounded poses. The top LEFT cell is frame1 and order is row-major. Carefully articulate actual jaws/legs/wings/tails; do NOT simply rotate/scale the entire animal as a substitute.  Exactly 4 COLUMNS by 2 ROWS (8 poses). Empty spaces must have ALPHA ZERO, never a white/grey sheet or grid. Input reference is STYLE ONLY, NOT rabbit anatomy or colours. A friendly full-body grey wolf, pale chest and muzzle, bushy tail. EIGHT HOWL poses: rest mouth closed, inhale chest, lift head/snouted muzzle upwards, head high mouth rounded open, hold howl with focussed gentle eyes, smaller mouth, lower head, rest. No aggression or bared scary teeth; expressive sustained sound posture.
